extracted.intended_audience: ACUS members, administrative law practitioners, agency staff, and members of the public interested in ACUS recommendations and administrative process reform
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the formal process and expectations for preparing, adopting, and implementing Recommendations (and occasional Statements) by the Administrative Conference of the United States. Covers who commissions studies, the form of reports, committee/Council/Assembly steps, and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory function: bring together public and private sectors to recommend improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations should aim to improve administrative and regulatory processes; this mission frames all study and recommendation activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement of consultants requires Council approval
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of ACUS’s Council, engages consultants to study particular administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiation of outside studies is a formal, Council-approved action led by the Office of the Chairman; Council approval is a procedural prerequisite to engaging consultants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive research report accompanied by suggested recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants then prepare a comprehensive research report accompanied by suggested recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations should be grounded in a comprehensive research report; suggested recommendations are expected to follow from the research findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACUS staff may prepare reports in-house
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally, ACUS staff members prepare these reports in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-house staff preparation is an acceptable alternative to consultant-prepared reports and follows the same downstream deliberative process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee adoption of proposed recommendations for Council consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: After extensive deliberation, committees of ACUS’s voting and non-voting members adopt proposed recommendations for Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee-level deliberation (including both voting and non-voting members) and formal committee adoption are steps required before Council review; extensive deliberation is expected at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council forwards recommendations, with its views, to the Assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council then forwards the recommendations, with its views, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council accompanies recommendations with its own views when transmitting them to the Assembly, indicating an evaluative/commentary role by the Council prior to Assembly action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly debate, amendment, and formal adoption (typically semi-annually)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly typically meets semi-annually in plenary session to debate, amend, and formally adopt the recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are considered at plenary Assembly sessions (generally twice a year) where debate and amendment are standard; formal adoption by the Assembly is the concluding deliberative step.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACUS undertakes to implement adopted recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS then undertakes to implement them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted recommendations are not merely advisory internal documents; ACUS takes steps toward implementation following Assembly adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of 'Statements' as an alternative to formal recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the Conference membership has acted to adopt a 'Statement' to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements generally follow the same process as recommendations but present issues, study conclusions, or comments rather than prescriptive recommendations; Statements are recorded in the searchable database (19 such Statements historically).
